task: Produce a fixed-horizon point forecast for each of many short, independent univariate series, submitted as one batch with no feedback between series.
objective: mean absolute error against held-out future values
data_characteristics: 137 independent series, no cross-series covariates and no exogenous features of any kind
42 to 47 observations of history per series; horizon is 5 steps
weekly aggregation of a physically driven quantity, so series carry a strong level and only weak within-window seasonality
series levels differ by orders of magnitude across the set
one shot: no validation feedback from the grader before the submission is final
bottlenecks: The best achievable constant forecast still falls far short of the published result, so effort spent choosing among constant rules is capped well below the target.
With under 50 observations per series, fitted models overfit and are hard to validate, which pushes attempts toward degenerate flat forecasts.
Series-level heterogeneity means a single globally chosen rule is wrong for part of the set.
extraction_focus: when a flat or last-value forecast is the wrong default despite short history, and what minimally beats it
how to decide per series whether to extrapolate level change rather than hold the level fixed
validating a forecasting choice on fewer than 50 observations without a held-out split
robust aggregation over a short window when the window contains outliers
